title: LLM-based NPCs in Video Games: A Systematic Mapping Study
title_zh: 电子游戏中的基于LLM的非玩家角色：一项系统映射研究

paragraphs.en: 对377篇文献开展系统映射研究，刻画LLM驱动的游戏NPC组件采用、延迟与安全现状，并识别商业化障碍。 For decades, non-player characters (NPCs) have been driven by rule-based systems whose personalities and interactions are scripted before release. Large language models (LLMs) promise NPCs that converse openly, adapt to new situations, and behave in ways developers did not fully author, prompting a wave of research and commercial experimentation. Yet the field lacks a unified picture of what has been built, how well it works, and at what cost. We address this gap with a systematic mapping study of 377 papers from the academic literature, yielding 42 papers analysed against a main research question and ten sub-questions across four thematic axes. We provide the first quantitative characterisation of component adoption, latency, safety coverage, and reproducibility: short-term memory and world-state grounding are near-universal (60% and 69%), whereas long-term memory (31%), reflection (38%), and retrieval-augmented generation (14%) remain rare, and response times span 2.6 to 15 seconds. Finally, we identify six structural barriers to commercial adoption and offer evidence-based recommendations for developers and researchers.
paragraphs.zh: 对377篇文献开展系统映射研究，刻画LLM驱动的游戏NPC组件采用、延迟与安全现状，并识别商业化障碍。几十年来，非玩家角色（NPC）一直由基于规则的系统驱动，其个性与交互在游戏发布前就已预先编写完成。 大语言模型（LLM）有望带来可以自由对话、适应新情境、并以开发者未完全预设的方式行事的NPC，由此引发了一波研究与商业化实验的浪潮。 然而，该领域仍然缺乏一幅统一的图景，说明已经构建了什么、效果如何、代价几何。 我们通过一项针对学术文献中377篇论文的系统映射研究来填补这一空白，最终围绕一个主要研究问题和十个子问题、横跨四个主题轴对42篇论文进行了分析。 我们首次对组件采用、延迟、安全覆盖与可复现性进行了定量刻画：短期记忆与世界状态接地已近乎普及（60%和69%），而长期记忆（31%）、反思（38%）和检索增强生成（14%）仍然少见，响应时间则在2.6至15秒之间。 最后，我们识别出阻碍商业化落地的六大结构性障碍，并为开发者和研究者提供了基于证据的建议。
